content:
Most students lose definite integration marks on the setup, not the calculus. Miss a symmetry or flip a limit, and a two minute problem eats ten. This free JEE Definite Integration online test puts that exact skill under pressure. It holds 15 MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer carries a short worked reason. So aim for 11 out of 15, then fix the gaps.

What JEE asks from Definite Integration

  • Property integrals using f of a plus b minus x.
  • Definite integrals read as the limit of a sum.
  • The fundamental theorem and derivatives of integral functions.
  • Area, plus physics like distance from acceleration.
  • Applied sums on cost, demand and water flow.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Integral of x from zero to one is one half.
  • Fold an integral with f of x equal to f of a plus b minus x.
  • For an odd function on minus a to a, the integral is zero.
  • The area under y equal to e to the x from zero to one is e minus one.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Splitting a modulus integral at the wrong point.
  • Forgetting to apply limits after substitution.
  • Dropping the chain rule in Leibniz differentiation.
  • Reading a geometric area as signed when it flips.

quiz.title: JEE Definite Integration Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If ∫₀¹ x dx = 1/2, then for any positive integer n, the value of ∫₀¹ xⁿ dx is

questions.explanation: Apply the f(x) → f(a−x) property and add the two forms. Then 2I = π/2, so I = π/4.
Use the a+b−x property with a+b = 5. Adding both forms gives 2I = 1, so I = 1/2.

questions.q: If f is continuous with f(x) = f(2a − x) for all x, and ∫₀^(2a) f(x) dx = I, then ∫₀^a f(x) dx equals
questions.explanation: Symmetry about x = a splits the integral into equal halves. So ∫₀^a f(x) dx = I/2.
The sum is a Riemann sum for ∫₀¹ x² dx, which equals 1/3.

questions.q: The points of extremum of f(x) = ∫₀ˣ t(t − 1)(t − 2) dt are
questions.explanation: By the fundamental theorem, f′(x) = x(x−1)(x−2). It vanishes at x = 0, 1 and 2.

questions.q: A train starts from rest with acceleration a(t) = 6t m/s². What distance does it cover in the first 2 seconds?
questions.explanation: Velocity v(t) = ∫6t dt = 3t². Distance = ∫₀² 3t² dt = [t³]₀² = 8 m.

questions.q: The area bounded by y = eˣ, the x-axis and the ordinate x = 1 is
questions.explanation: Area = ∫₀¹ eˣ dx = e¹ − e⁰ = e − 1.

questions.q: The marginal cost is MC = 100 + 2x, where x is the number of units. Find the added cost of raising output from 10 to 20 units.
The demand function is p(x) = 100 − x². If the equilibrium quantity is 6, find the consumer surplus at price p(6).
What is the value of ∫₀¹ 1/(1 + x²) dx?
questions.explanation: The antiderivative is tan⁻¹x. So the value is tan⁻¹1 − tan⁻¹0 = π/4.

questions.q: Water flows into a tank at rate R(t) = 10e^(0.2t) litres per minute. How much is added in the first 5 minutes?

questions.explanation: The antiderivative is sin⁻¹x. So the value is sin⁻¹1 − sin⁻¹0 = π/2.

questions.q: Evaluate ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx.
questions.explanation: Use f(x) → f(a−x) and add the two forms. Then 2I = π/2, so I = π/4.
